Installation and operation

The repository-root README contains the full copy-and-paste commands for both virtual-environment and Docker setup. It is the authoritative setup guide.

Virtual environment

Clone the public repository, change into it, create a virtual environment, install requirements-dev.txt, and copy newsroom/.env.example to newsroom/.env. Generate your own secret key and choose database credentials. Install MariaDB, create a database and user as documented, then run migrations and runserver from the newsroom directory.

The default Docker route creates MariaDB through Compose and needs no local Python or MariaDB installation. A SQLite-only demonstration can be selected explicitly in the environment for quick local inspection.

Docker

Copy .env.docker.example to .env at the repository root. Replace the secret key, database password and database root password with independent random values. Run docker compose up --build -d and open http://localhost:8000. The database has a named volume and its healthcheck must pass before the web container migrates and starts. The web app runs as a non-root account and serves static files with WhiteNoise.

Stop the stack with docker compose down. This preserves database storage. Removing volumes destroys data, so it is not part of normal shutdown.

Documentation

From the repository root with build dependencies installed:

python -m sphinx -b html newsroom/docs newsroom/docs/_build/html -W

Open newsroom/docs/_build/html/index.html. The generated HTML is deliberately tracked so visitors can read it without installing Sphinx. The configuration sets DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE and calls django.setup() before autodoc imports the models. Documentation uses a database-free SQLite configuration; it does not need your MariaDB password or a running server.
